item.title: Noah Kahan Earns First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘The Great Divide’
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to this week's music update. We're diving into the latest from the Billboard 200 chart, where a new album has taken the top spot.
[Short music transition]
Host: Noah Kahan's fourth full-length studio project, "The Great Divide", has debuted at number one, earning an impressive 389,000 equivalent album units in the United States. This marks Kahan's biggest week by units, and it's also the largest week for a rock album since the chart started measuring by units in 2014.
[Short music transition]
Host: But that's not all - "The Great Divide" has also achieved the largest streaming week of any album in 2026, with over 215 million on-demand streams. And, it claims the biggest vinyl sales week for a rock album in the modern era, with 118,000 copies sold.
[Short music transition]
Host: This isn't Kahan's first time on the chart, though. His previous album, "Stick Season", peaked at number two in 2024, and it's now back in the top 10. Other notable entries this week include Kehlani's self-titled album at number four, and Michael Jackson's "Thriller" re-entering the chart at number seven.
[Short music transition]
Host: The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week based on multi-metric consumption, including album sales, track equivalent albums, and streaming equivalent albums. We'll have to wait until May 5th to see the full chart, but for now, it's clear that Noah Kahan's "The Great Divide" is making waves in the music world.
[Outro music starts]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to this week's music update. Follow us for more chart news and updates, and we'll catch you in the next episode.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
